title: Fit lids onto cable tray meeting in middle
instruction: Close the cable tray with both teal lids.
setup: Dual YAM embodiment at ready on station tabletop. Steel-grey cable tray (120 mm wide in x, 400 mm long in y, 60 mm high, 25 kg, friction 1.2, fixed in place) centred at x=30 cm, y=0 whose two 15 mm thick, 60 mm high side walls act as the rails the lids rest on. Two teal lids (118x196x12 mm as x by y by height, 0.3 kg each, friction 0.6) with a 40x80x10 mm handle on top of each lie on two 120x220x10 mm side pads centred at x=16 cm, y=+22 cm and y=-22 cm. Real build: the tray is bent 3 mm steel sheet bolted to the table (this replaces the 25 kg fixed mass); the lids are 12 mm thick solid PETG slabs, each with a 3D-printed PETG handle (40x80x10 mm) glued on; the side pads are 5 mm PETG plates. Material as modelled: every object is a rigid body with only the size, mass and friction stated here; nothing deforms, and nothing snaps or latches except through contact and the listed slider springs.
scoring: Ladder: 0.25 one lid on the rails, 0.50 both lids on the rails, 0.75 lids near the centre (gap <= 6 cm), 1.00 lids meet flush (gap <= 5 mm, height difference <= 3 mm) and motionless for 1.0 s. A lid is on the rails when its centre is within 25 mm of x = 300 mm and within 8 mm of 63 mm above the tabletop, so a lid held above its seat does not count. Gate: tray drift > 5 mm zeroes score. Possible scores: 0.0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0.
fidelity: Fixed heavy 25 kg trough fixture with guide rails. Lids are loose rigid bodies with 0.6 friction. Scorer evaluates physical 3D contact, gap width, and flushness.
context: Datacenter technicians and cable installers enclose high-density fiber runs within protected cable trays (O*NET 49-2022.00, 49-9052.00).
reset_notes: Return lids to staging pads at x=16 cm. Verify cable tray is fixed at x=30 cm.
